# The proposal
<!--
How are you going to solve the problem? Include the concrete actions you
will take and an estimated timeline. What are likely failure modes and
how will you recover from them?

This is where the proposal should be outlined.
-->

This proposal is to fund the completion of the R package, {geoarrowrs}, which is a geoarrow-native compute engine for the R ecosystem.

The R package will provide memory efficient and parallelized implementation for geometric operations out of the box.
In addition, it will provide advanced spatial join and query operations.
The R package will integrate into the existing ecosystem with a focus on integration with {arrow}, {dplyr}, and {sf} to minimize friction in adoption.

This proposal is for work in the following

1. Core geometry algorithm implementation
2. Parallelization and
3. {sf} integration

"sf is slow"
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78009568/slow-performance-on-r-spatial-distance-calculation
https://jacobbradt.com/blog/2022/spatialbatch/
https://www.researchgate.net/post/How_to_speed_up_spatial_operations_with_R_sf_package
improvements via https://github.com/r-spatial/sf/issues/1925

geos has historically been the fastest R package in the ecosystem  but was very low level and not widely used
geoarrow became a standard in 2023 and its first major spec announced in 2025 https://geoarrow.org/news/release-0-2.html

This package aims to be faster than geos, competitive with duckspatial and sedonadb, and as ergonomic as {sf} (with a drop in replacement via `mask_sf()`)
for **in memory** computation

- Core R package:

        - Sort-tile-recursive
    - Spatial Joins
        - All basic spatial predictates
        - KNN join
        - Distance Joins
    - Full coverage of all geometric operations in georust/geo
- {arrow} R package registered user defined functions
- sf compatibility S3 method registration
- CRS propagation?

### Readers

- provided by geoarrow for geosjons and flatgeobuf
- shapefile needs manual im

### Algorithm Implementation

- Relying on geo for core geometric operation algorithms
- Joins are hand crafted used both geo and geo-index for creating query trees

### Architecture

<!--
What does the high-level architecture look like?
-->

- Rust based R package via [extendr](https://github.com/extendr/extendr)
- Arrow FFI between R and Rust via [arrow-extendr](https://github.com/extendr/arrow-extendr)
- Native algorithms using [geo](https://docs.rs/geo)
- Spatial Indexing using geo-index
- Readers and writer using:
    - geozero https://docs.rs/crate/geozero/0.14.0
    - geojson
    - flatgeobuf
- Parallelism via https://docs.rs/rayon
